subject: Infra decision mapping: SSO, KMS/HSM, log retention — next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Infra decision mapping: SSO, KMS/HSM, log retention — next steps

Elaine — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what will drive Private vs Dedicated for SilverLine: 

Recap of decision drivers we heard today
- SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning required for user mapping and provisioning.
- KMS/HSM: Compliance requires HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) for certain PHI-related workloads.
- Logging: 7-year immutable retention for audit logs and exportable access logs for regulators.
- Network: VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress for inference traffic.

What this means from a product fit perspective
- Hosted API: fast to onboard but cannot meet HSM requirement or guarantee customer-managed HSM; logs retention limited by hosted plan SLAs.
- Dedicated capacity: supports customer-managed cloud KMS (BYOK) and SAML/SCIM integrations in most cases, but does not provide customer HSM appliance access. Log retention can be extended but may still be constrained by multi-tenant control plane policies.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): supports customer-controlled HSM, longer retention windows, private control plane and full audit access — aligns best with the requirements you described.

Attachments: I pulled together a short evidence checklist and a blank mapping sheet to capture your exact requirements.
[Attachment: redwood-infra-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
[Attachment: slh-ssoreqs.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)]

Proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm the HSM certification level and the security team contact who owns the KMS/HSM decision? (action: Elaine)
2) Technical deep dive (30–45m) with our infra security and runtime team to validate network and log export options — suggested times: Wed 6/9 10:00 or Thu 6/10 14:00 PT. (action: Markus / Soojin to schedule)
3) We’ll prepare a short comparison matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with gaps and estimated delta for procurement and ops. (action: Redwood)

If you prefer, we can treat the initial technical deep-dive as a lightweight PoC scoping session (no code) to confirm whether Dedicated could be made acceptable with compensating controls or whether Private is required.

Thanks — Mark

Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Infra decision mapping: SSO, KMS/HSM, log retention — next steps

Markus — thanks for the summary and the files. A few clarifications from our side: 
- HSM: We do require HSM-backed key management for production PHI workflows; compliance team specified FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent.
- SSO: Okta SAML for auth + SCIM for user provisioning. We must enforce role mappings to our internal groups on day one.
- Logs: Retention is 7 years; we also need the ability to export raw audit logs to our archival system on a weekly cadence.
- Network: VPC peering is preferred; PrivateLink is acceptable if it supports the same egress controls.

We can make Wed 6/9 10:00 PT work for a technical deep dive. Security will be on the call (copying our IT alias).

Also: please include a short note on whether Dedicated could be augmented (e.g., partner HSM, customer-managed cloud KMS + attestation) or if Private is the only path. That will steer procurement.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of IT Operations, SilverLine Health
elaine.park@silverlinehealth.com | +1 617-555-2224

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra decision mapping: SSO, KMS/HSM, log retention — next steps

Elaine / Markus — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive.

Short answer: Private is the cleanest path to satisfy all three asks (HSM, 7yr retention, VPC peering).
Why: 
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Dedicated supports BYOK via major cloud KMS providers (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and can attest to key ownership, but those managed KMS offerings do not provide a customer-operated HSM appliance that meets FIPS Level 3 hardware requirements. If SilverLine’s compliance team requires an on-prem or HSM-backed HSM appliance (e.g., Luna/HSM appliance with direct control), Dedicated cannot give that hardware-level control. Private (VPC or on-prem package) allows integration with customer HSM appliances or colocated HSMs.
- SSO: Both Dedicated and Private support SAML + SCIM. Dedicated can integrate with Okta for provisioning and role sync; we should capture exact attribute mappings.
- Logs: We can extend log retention on Dedicated but the control plane (for hosted elements) may still have limits around immutable retention and export. Private gives you full control over storage lifecycle and immutable archives for 7 years.

Compensating controls for Dedicated (if you want to explore)
- Customer-managed cloud KMS keys (CMEK) with strict key rotation and attestation, plus contractual controls and periodic audits.
- Signed attestation + HSM-backed HSM from a vetted cloud provider (if the compliance team accepts cloud HSM with appropriate assurances).

For the deep-dive on Wed 6/9 10:00 PT I propose the following agenda:
- 10:00 — quick intro + objectives (Markus)
- 10:05 — SilverLine security requirements walk-through (Elaine / Security)
- 10:15 — Redwood infra capabilities: KMS options, HSM constraints, SSO/SCIM mapping (Soojin)
- 10:30 — Logs & retention export patterns (Olga)
- 10:40 — Next steps & procurement implications (Markus)

Markus: I’ll prepare a short one-page comparison table (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and bring concrete notes on what Dedicated can and cannot provide WRT HSM.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Great — Wed 6/9 10:00 PT confirmed. Will send calendar invite and include a short prep packet (comparison table + evidence checklist).

Immediate asks before the call (can you please respond by EOD Tue?):
- Elaine / security: short bullet list of absolute MUST-HAVES vs nice-to-have for the PoC (makes the tradeoffs clear).
- Procurement: any required contract language for BYOK / KMS escrow / data residency that we should pre-load into the conversation.

Soojin: thanks — please attach the comparison table and a one-page note on Dedicated gap areas (HSM specifics + log immutability constraints) to the invite. Olga: please prepare the log export patterns we support and the expected retention deltas and cost impact.

If it looks like Private is required, we’ll flag procurement early so they can size the estimated delta and timeline. Otherwise we’ll document compensating controls and draft a compliance attestation for your review.

Thanks everyone — Mark
